version.changelog:
Version 1.0.5 of "aicreditshare-platform" is a major update with a complete documentation and structure overhaul.

- Replaced English README and technical workflow with detailed Chinese documentation in SKILL.md, focusing on end-to-end platform scenarios and API usage.
- Added new files: README.md, _meta.json, and scripts/aics.sh, scripts/init.sh.
- Removed legacy script files and old API/reference documentation (12 files deleted).
- SKILL.md now describes user-centric workflows (注册、发布/接任务、技能雇佣、余额查询) with sample API calls and step-by-step explanations.
- Emphasis on HMAC signature authentication, score rules, and practical platform cases for agents and skill marketplace.

llm.summary: The skill's purpose (automating an AI Credit Share platform) matches the code and docs, but the package omits declared dependencies, writes API credentials to a plaintext file in the user's home, and uses hard-coded passwords — those mismatches and storage practices merit caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, SKILL.md, README, and scripts all target the same https://www.aicreditshare.com APIs and the provided endpoints are consistent with the stated capabilities. However the skill metadata and runtime files do not declare required command-line tools (curl, jq, openssl) even though scripts depend on them.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits runtime to HTTP but the included scripts read and write ~/.aicreditshare/config.json (creating persistent credentials), perform HMAC signing locally, and rely on shell utilities. The instructions and scripts therefore access the user's home filesystem and persist secrets — behavior not declared in requires.* and broader than a pure HTTP-only instruction set.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which reduces installer risk. But the repo includes executable shell scripts that, when run, create files under the user's home directory (~/.aicreditshare). Installing or running those scripts will cause local state to be written to disk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential, yet the scripts register/login and save agentApiKey/agentApiSecret (and token) to a plaintext config file in the home directory. The init script also uses a hard-coded password ('Test123456') for register/login calls — suspicious practice and poor credential hygiene given the skill's scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill does persist credentials to ~/.aicreditshare/config.json and will reuse them for subsequent requests, giving it ongoing access to the user's platform account until the file is deleted. It does not request elevated system privileges or modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (automating actions on aicreditshare.com) but has several practical red flags: 1) the shipped scripts require curl, jq, and openssl though the skill doesn't declare them — ensure these are available and review their usage before running; 2) init.sh will register or log in and save API keys/secrets and tokens in plaintext at ~/.aicreditshare/config.json — treat that file as sensitive and consider whether you accept storing credentials unencrypted on disk; 3) the registration/login flow in the scripts uses a hard-coded password ('Test123456'), which is insecure and may not be intended for production; 4) verify the API base URL and TLS identity of https://www.aicreditshare.com yourself before creating accounts or sending credentials; 5) if you decide to use the skill, run it in an isolated account or sandbox, inspect the scripts line-by-line, and remove the saved config when finished (rm ~/.aicreditshare/config.json). If you need higher assurance, ask the author for signed releases or a version that uses secure credential storage (OS keyring) and removes hard-coded passwords.
